scope: Mechanism hypotheses, not assumed source-label truth. All six selections retained; unknown is not positional. No score input is fabricated.
variants: Every legal source ply retained at its actual ply; no later motif promoted to the root without an independent root certificate
contracts: Claims must have legally connected targets and account for initiating sacrifices and recaptures.
A later conditional gain must not outrank an independently proved root cause merely because of its material number.
Named mate and promotion require legal terminal geometry or explicit forced proof; silver labels alone do not establish them.
Counterfactual controls are explanatory probes, not independent public examples.

cases.hypothesis: Rg8 interposes on Re8-to-Nh8 and threatens the knight and promotion route. Check whether rook/knight escapes invalidate a forced material claim; do not infer interference from geometry alone.
cases.contrary: Remove the h7 promotion pawn or change the knight's legal escape support; distinguish direct loose capture from a coupled promotion threat.

cases.hypothesis: Rh3+ may induce the king to block its own second-rank rook defence, allowing Rh2+ and Rxa2. Enumerate every king evasion; do not infer a forced skewer from only Kf2.
cases.contrary: Keep an alternative evasion or remove the rear rook. A later king-front skewer belongs to its actual ply unless independently forced from Rh3.

cases.hypothesis: Rf3+ and Rxc2+ appear to drive the white king away from Nb3, followed by Rxb3. Verify every evasion and account for both black rooks and counterchecks.
cases.contrary: Remove Nb3 or its original king guard and check whether supposed deflection depends on that exact target rather than unrelated pawn collection.

cases.hypothesis: f7+ and gxh7 threaten promotion while attacking the knight's defensive arrangement. A short source line does not independently prove promotion or deflection; check all check evasions including queen intervention.
cases.contrary: Remove the second pawn or supply a legal promotion blocker; abstain if the longer ending is not certified.

cases.hypothesis: Ne2+ Kh1 Rxh2+ Kxh2 Rh8# suggests forced Anastasia mate and attraction of the king. Verify every legal check evasion; material fork/discovery noise must not displace forced mate.
cases.contrary: Remove the mating knight or provide a legal king escape; distinguish mating support from incidental bishop/rook attacks.

cases.hypothesis: Rxe4 fxe4 Rf1+ Rxf1 g2+ Kh2 gxf1=N+ suggests an underpromotion fork after two sacrifices. Test alternatives to accepting either rook, exact material debt, and the final knight's actual targets.
cases.contrary: Remove a fork victim or promotion support. A later underpromotion branch must not be mistaken for a proved root mechanism solely because the source line contains it.
